item.title: What next? Kurds say yes, Druze still say no to united Syria
item.description: The Druze minority in Sweida, Syria, is now the only group that hasn't accepted central government authority. How does the end of an independent Kurdish area impact Druze plans for a different, divided kind of Syria?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Uganda: World's 'youngest monarch' dies aged 34
item.description: Oyo Nyimba, once recognized as the world's youngest reigning monarch, has died in his mid-30s. As one of Uganda's traditional monarchs, he took the throne of the Tooro kingdom in 1995, aged just 3.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Africa's aging autocrats fight to stay in power
item.description: As some of Africa's longest-serving leaders grow older, they are using different tactics to extend their rule. But age, succession battles and public pressure pose new challenges.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Serbia: Keeping EU, Russia in play ahead of key election
item.description: As Serbia heads towards an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room to maneuver.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: South Korea leans toward military conscription for women
item.description: Facing a population decline, fewer potential service members and calls for social equality to be extended to national military service, Korea is inching closer to breaking the taboo on women on the front line.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: India's citizen-led school audits test limits of activism
item.description: The student-led "Cockroach" movement is taking its campaign for accountability to government schools, but the activists' methods are encountering growing resistance from authorities.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Nepal-Tibet flood deaths pass 500, thousands still missing
item.description: The Red Cross says more than 93,000 people are affected by the deadly floods and landslides on the China-Nepal border. Rescue efforts were temporarily paused after an overflowing lake threatened to trigger more floods.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Norway's King Harald dies at 89
item.description: King Harald is succeeded by his son, who has taken the name King Haakon VIII, with Crown Princess Mette-Marit now queen.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Protesters set fire to migrant camp in Ceuta
item.description: The unrest comes one month after a mass influx of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish exclave in North Africa.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Spain: Thieves steal Bronze Age gold in lightning raid on Villena Museum
item.description: One of the world's greatest Bronze Age gold collections has been swiped, almost in its entirety, from Villena Museum. A highly professional group of thieves were in and out in four minutes flat before the museum opened.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: The man behind Srebrenica: Ratko Mladic dies at 84
item.description: For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian War. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and of other war crimes. Now he has died in detention at The Hague.
